speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you tell me if you have experienced any recent head trauma, neck stiffness, or confusion prior to this fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of taking haloperidol and the sudden onset of fever and altered mentation, have you noticed any muscle rigidity, excessive sweating, or elevated blood pressure? I would like to request a Complete Blood Count and a Creatine Kinase level to check for signs of infection or muscle breakdown.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any autonomic instability, such as labile blood pressure, tachycardia, or dilated pupils? I would also like to check your current temperature and vital signs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of fever, severe generalized rigidity, altered mental status, autonomic instability (profuse sweating), and significantly elevated creatine kinase in a patient on haloperidol is classic for Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
